PRAYING TO a) SET ASIDE THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 15.10.2020 PASSED IN MVC NO.634/2014 BY THE MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL NO.XIII, AT VIJAYAPURA; b) PASS SUCH OTHER ORDERS/RELIEFS AS THIS HON'BLE COURT DEEMS FIT AND PROPER IN THE FACTS CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE.

THESE MFAs HAVING BEEN HEARD AND RESERVED FOR JUDGMENT ON 07.02.2023, COMING ON FOR PRONOUNCEMENT OF JUDGMENT THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:-
 JUDGMENT

These two appeals are arising out of judgment and award dated 15.10.2020 in MVC No.634/2014 on the file of Motor Vehicle Accidents Claims Tribunal No.XIII, Vijayapur, by which the Tribunal partly allowed the claim petition granting compensation in a sum of Rs.12,64,893/- with interest at 9% p.a.
and directed respondent No.3 to pay the same.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. While MFA No.201668/2021 is filed by petitioners seeking enhancement, MFA No.201002/2021 is filed by respondent No.3-Insurance Company to dismiss the claim petition on the ground that the accident was caused by a Truck and in order to claim compensation through respondent No.3

,
petitioners have falsely involved Tractor bearing registration No.KA-28/TB-1125 and trailers bearing registration Nos.KA-28/TB-1127 and KA-29/T-3375 ('the offending vehicle' for short) which were covered by a valid policy issued by respondent No.3.
3. Since these two appeals are arising out of the same judgment and award, they are clubbed together and are decided by a common order.
4. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
5. FACTS:

Brief facts leading to filing of the claim petition are that the petitioners are the husband,
sons and mother-in-law of the deceased-Gangawwa.

On 27.01.2014, at about 5.00 p.m., the deceased-Gangawwa was standing in front of her house abutting National Highway No.218 connecting Vijayapura - Bagalkot near Upper Krishna Project Cross Road, Kolhar.

At that time,
offending vehicle driven by its driver-Mallappa Parasappa Ukkali came in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against the deceased.
As a result of the accident, deceased sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, she was shifted to Sanjeevini Hospital Vijayapura.
From there she was taken to Yeshodhara Super Speciality Hospital, Solapur of Maharashtra State.

However, she succumbed to Gireppa @ Giriyappa And Ors vs Maruthi And Ors on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/1853941/
4 injuries on 28.01.2014 at about 3.00 a.m.

sentences.text: 5.1 Deceased was aged about 35 years.
She was earning Rs.7,500/- per month.
Petitioners were dependent on her income.
As the owners of offending vehicle, respondent Nos.1 and 2 and as insurer, respondent No.3 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
6. Despite due service of notice, respondent Nos.1 and 2 have remained exparte before the Tribunal.
7. Respondent No.3 appeared and filed written statement denying and disputing the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident.

The offending vehicle has been falsely implicated to make wrongful gain as the accident was caused by a Truck and since either petitioner could not trace out the said Truck or it was not duly insured, the offending vehicle has been implicated by the petitioners in collusion with concerned police as well as respondent Nos.1 and 2.

Respondent No.3 has also disputed the age, income of the deceased and that petitioners were dependent on her and as such entitled for compensation and has sought for dismissal of the petition against respondent No.3.
8.
Based on these pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.
9. In support of Petitioners' claim, petitioner Nos.1 and 2 are examined as PW-1 and PW-2.

They have relied upon Exs.P-1 to P-12.
10.
On behalf of Respondent No.3, one witness is examined as RW-1 and Exs.R-1 to R-4 are marked.
11. Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition granting compensation in a sum of Rs.12,64,893/- with interest at 9% p.a.

The details of compensation is as under:
Heads Amount 1st 2nd 3rd 4th In Rs. petitioner petitioner petitioner petitioner Loss of 10,20,000 2,70,000 3,75,000 3,75,000 NIL income or financial dependency Loss of 1,00,000 1,00,000 NIL NIL NIL spousal consortium Parental 80,000 NIL 40,000 40,000 NIL Consortium Medical 39,893 39,893 NIL NIL NIL expenses Transportati 25,000 25,000 NIL NIL NIL on & Funeral Total 12,64,893 4,34,893 4,15,000 4,15,000 NIL 12.

Respondent No.3 has filed MFA No.201002/2021 contending that the Tribunal has erred in fastening the liability on respondent No.3 without proper appreciation of materials placed on record resulting in miscarriage of justice.
It has failed to appreciate that the offending vehicle is not at all involved in the alleged accident.
As per the MLC intimation sent to the Police by the Yashodhara Super Speciality Hospital Pvt. Ltd., Solapur, the deceased was hit by a Truck.

entities.text: Yashodhara Super Speciality Hospital Pvt. Ltd., Solapur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In the Police Diary also the fact of accident being caused by an unknown Truck is forthcoming.

However, the Tribunal has failed to appreciate that the concerned police in collusion with the claimants and insured owner of the offending vehicle have falsely implicated the offending vehicle to claim compensation from respondent No.3.
Though the alleged incident took place on 27.01.2014, the complaint came to be lodged on 05.02.2014 giving room for the claimants and the concerned police to falsely implicate the offending vehicle.
The Tribunal has failed to appreciate that it is a fraudulent claim made by the petitioners against respondent No.3 to make wrongful gain.

sentences.text: At the time of accident, deceased was aged below 40 years.
Therefore, compensation under the head future prospects at the rate of 40% was required to be added.
The compensation granted under other heads is also on the lower side and prays to allow the appeal and enhance the compensation accordingly.

15. Heard arguments and perused the record.
16.

Thus, respondent No.3 has challenged the impugned judgment and award contending that the accident in question was caused by a Truck, but for obvious i.e., either it is a case of hit and run and as such, petitioners were not aware of the registration number of the Truck which caused accident or that it was not covered by valid insurance, they as an after thought in collusion with the concerned police have falsely implicated the offending vehicle which is obviously covered by a valid policy issued by respondent No.3.
AIR 1985 SC 106 17.

In order to establish this aspect, respondent No.3 has relied upon MLC report submitted by the Sanjeevini Hospital, Vijayapura as well as at the earliest available opportunity, i.e., while filing the written statement, respondent No.3 has specifically contended that accident is not caused by the offending vehicle.

On the other hand, it may be an unknown vehicle and as an after thought,
petitioners have specifically implicated the offending vehicle to see that the compensation is paid by respondent No.3, since the offending vehicle is covered by policy issued by it.
In the light of the same, heavy burden is on the petitioners to prove that the accident was caused by the offending vehicle and to remove any doubt as to its non involvement.

18. It is not in dispute that at the first instance, the deceased was admitted to Sanjeevini Hospital,
Vijayapura.
From there she was shifted to Yashodhara Super Specialty Hospital Pvt.Ltd., Solapur.

sentences.text: fact, Sanjeevini Hospital has also sent an MLC to the Adarsh Nagar Police about the admission of deceased with history of road traffic accident.
The MLC report is available at page 57 of the TCR.
It bears endorsement by the concerned Police for having received the original.
It appears that the concerned Police have not acted upon the said MLC report.

It also appears that since the deceased was shifted to the Yashodhara Super Specialty Hospital Pvt. Ltd., Solapur, Adarsh Nagar Police might not have been able to get the statement of the relatives of the deceased to register the case.

sentences.text: 19. Ex.R-2 is the MLC report sent by the Yashodhara Super Speciality Hospital Pvt. Ltd., Solapur to the Jail Road Police Station, Solapur regarding the admission and subsequent death of deceased.

entities.text: Yashodhara Super Speciality Hospital Pvt. Ltd., Solapur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In fact it states that immediately after the admission of the deceased, a MLC was sent to the concerned Police in MLC No.4640 and this is the second MLC report sent by the said Hospital after the death of the deceased.
In this document, it is stated that the history of injury was given as deceased was hit by a Truck at UKP cross, Kolhar of Bagewadi Taluk.
20. Based on the report, the concerned Police have made entry in the Station House Diary as per Ex.R-3, the Kannada translation of which is at Ex.R-3(a).

This entry also states that the deceased was hit by a Truck and she was initially admitted to Sanjeevini Hospital, Vijayapura and from there she was brought to Yashodhara Super Speciality Hospital Pvt. Ltd., Solapur and while undergoing treatment, she succumbed to the injuries.

entities.text: Yashodhara Super Speciality Hospital Pvt. Ltd., Solapur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 21. Ex.P-1 is the First Information Report registered by the concerned police, namely, Kolhar Police Station on 05.02.2014 in Crime No.22/2014.
This case is registered based on the transfer of the case registered by the Solapur, Jail Road Police on the point of jurisdiction.

In other words based on the MLC report given by the Yashodhara Super Speciality Hospital Pvt. Ltd., Solapur, it appears that the Solapur Jail Road Police have registered a case and subsequently, on the point of jurisdiction, they have transferred the case to the Kolhar Police Station.

entities.text: Yashodhara Super Speciality Hospital Pvt. Ltd., Solapur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Petitioners have not produced the complaint filed before the Jail Road Police Station, Solapur as well as the FIR registered by the said Police.
Consequently, neither the Tribunal nor this Court is in a position to know what was the statement given before the said Police and against whom the said case was registered.

22. In the light of the specific statement made in the MLC report at Ex.R-2 as well as Ex.R-3 wherein it is stated that the deceased was hit by a Truck, it was obligatory on the part of the petitioner to produce the copy of the complaint as well as the FIR registered by the Jai Road Police, Solapur, to ascertain what was the complaint that was filed before the said Police.

Respondent No.3 has taken up specific defence that though the accident was caused by a Truck, registration number of which is not forthcoming, which may be a case of hit and run or a case where the said vehicle was not covered by a valid policy, it was obligatory on the part of the petitioners to come clear with their case.

23. Despite, respondent No.3 taking up a specific defence and placing on record the documents which contradict the claim of the petitioners that accident was caused by offending vehicle, the Tribunal has ignored the important evidence by observing that respondent No.3 has not challenged the charge sheet filed by the concerned Police.

Even if such charge sheet is challenged before this Court, usually they will be disposed of with an observation that the concerned person is at liberty to counter the veracity of the charge sheet during the trial.
When the Sanjeevini Hospital as well as Gireppa @ Giriyappa And Ors vs Maruthi And Ors on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/1853941/

sentences.text: 7 Yashodhara Super Speciality Hospital Pvt. Ltd., Solapur, Hospital authorities have sent the MLC report at the earliest point of time, there is no explanation by the petitioners or the concerned Police as to why case was not registered immediately.

entities.text: Yashodhara Super Speciality Hospital Pvt. Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: There is inordinate delay of nearly 8 days in filing the complaint and registering the case.
Obviously, this gave opportunity to the petitioners as well as the concerned Police to manipulate record.
24. It may be true that petitioners were busy in getting the treatment to the deceased on 27.01.2014 and 28.01.2014.
However, since deceased is having husband and two adult sons, atleast one of them could have filed complaint immediately.
Obviously, the concerned Hospital authorities have got information through the persons who accompanied the deceased to the Hospital.
Petitioners owe an explanation as to why such information was given to the Hospital authorities at the earliest point of time.

Without such information being furnished by the persons who accompanied the injured,
obviously, the concerned Hospital Authorities were not in a position to give such information to the concerned Police through the MLC report.
25. Ignoring all these aspects, the Tribunal has brushed aside the specific defence taken by respondent No.3.
Atleast the petitioners could have lead additional evidence by producing the complaint and FIR registered by the Jail Road Police, Solapur which came to be transferred to Kolhar Police.
In the light of decisions relied upon the respondent No.3, it is obvious that the claim made by petitioners against respondent No.3 is a fraudulent claim.

Though the accident is caused by a Truck, the registration number of which is not being disclosed or it is case of hit and run,
petitioners have implicated the offending vehicle solely for the reason that it is covered by Policy issued by respondent No.3.
26.
In the light of the above discussion, this Court is of the considered opinion that the claim petition against respondent No.3 is not tenable and liable to be dismissed.

When the claim petition is itself liable to be dismissed, the question of entertaining the appeal filed by the petitioners for enhancement of the compensation would not arise and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) MFA No.201002/2021 filed by respondent No.3/Insurance Company
is allowed.
In the result, MVC No.634/2014 on the file of Motor Vehicle Accidents Claims Tribunal No.XIII, Vijayapur is dismissed.

opennyai_summary.facts:
As a result of the accident, deceased sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, she was shifted to Sanjeevini Hospital Vijayapura.
Respondent No.3 has filed MFA No.201002/2021 contending that the Tribunal has erred in fastening the liability on respondent No.3 without proper appreciation of materials placed on record resulting in miscarriage of justice.
It has failed to appreciate that the offending vehicle is not at all involved in the alleged accident.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The Tribunal has failed to appreciate that it is a fraudulent claim made by the petitioners against respondent No.3 to make wrongful gain.
. On the other hand, petitioners have challenged the impugned judgment and award contending that the Tribunal has not granted any compensation under the head shadow of death as held in N.
Sivammal and Others Vs. Managing Director, Pandian Roadways Corporation AIR 2000 SC 1165 (1994) 1 SCC 1 1996 (5) SCC 550 2005 (5) Karnataka Law Journal 295 and Another (Sivammal's case)5.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In order to establish this aspect, respondent No.3 has relied upon MLC report submitted by the Sanjeevini Hospital, Vijayapura as well as at the earliest available opportunity, i.e., while filing the written statement, respondent No.3 has specifically contended that accident is not caused by the offending vehicle.
On the other hand, it may be an unknown vehicle and as an after thought,
petitioners have specifically implicated the offending vehicle to see that the compensation is paid by respondent No.3, since the offending vehicle is covered by policy issued by it.
In the light of the same, heavy burden is on the petitioners to prove that the accident was caused by the offending vehicle and to remove any doubt as to its non involvement.

6
23. Despite, respondent No.3 taking up a specific defence and placing on record the documents which contradict the claim of the petitioners that accident was caused by offending vehicle, the Tribunal has ignored the important evidence by observing that respondent No.3 has not challenged the charge sheet filed by the concerned Police.
Even if such charge sheet is challenged before this Court, usually they will be disposed of with an observation that the concerned person is at liberty to counter the veracity of the charge sheet during the trial.
However, since deceased is having husband and two adult sons, atleast one of them could have filed complaint immediately.
Obviously, the concerned Hospital authorities have got information through the persons who accompanied the deceased to the Hospital.
Petitioners owe an explanation as to why such information was given to the Hospital authorities at the earliest point of time.
Without such information being furnished by the persons who accompanied the injured,
obviously, the concerned Hospital Authorities were not in a position to give such information to the concerned Police through the MLC report.
Atleast the petitioners could have lead additional evidence by producing the complaint and FIR registered by the Jail Road Police, Solapur which came to be transferred to Kolhar Police.
Though the accident is caused by a Truck, the registration number of which is not being disclosed or it is case of hit and run,
petitioners have implicated the offending vehicle solely for the reason that it is covered by Policy issued by respondent No.3.

opennyai_summary.decision:
When the claim petition is itself liable to be dismissed, the question of entertaining the appeal filed by the petitioners for enhancement of the compensation would not arise and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) MFA No.201002/2021 filed by respondent No.3/Insurance Company
is allowed.
In the result, MVC No.634/2014 on the file of Motor Vehicle Accidents Claims Tribunal No.XIII, Vijayapur is dismissed.
ii) Consequently, MFA No.201668/2021 filed by the petitioners is also dismissed.
iii) Respondent No.3/Insurance Company is at liberty withdraw the amount in deposit (if any).
 iv) The Registry is directed to transmit the trial  Court records along with copy of this  judgment to the Tribunal forthwith.
